chapter: Records and playing in New Orleans
title: A jam session with Andrew Morgan and Cap
summary: He remembers a jam session or recording with Andrew Morgan and Cap, and a time of fraternity parties.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: What was that some long ago? Mmm...
I just remember how long it was. It must have been probably... Well, was this at my house or two hundred? No, it was at two hundred...

They had Andrew Morgan, they had Cap, Homer Eugene, and I just remember, they had two men, about four or five, and they were recording or doing something. It wasn't for long, it was just something that he wanted did, you know, that they wanted did, and it wasn't long because I brought Cap up there because Cap didn't know, you know, the city, he didn't know how to get up there, it was, and so we went up there. Tell me what that was. It must have been before my time. That was during your time because you had... Well, Cap used to work at two lines. I know, but Cap wasn't working there then. Yeah. Because you had, you played piano, you played...
Lawrence, yeah, Lawrence was there. It must have been some sort of jam session. Yeah, some little jam session. Yeah, I might have... Yeah, it was a jam session up there.
Something like that. That's what it was, the jam session.
Yeah, it was jam session. It might have been.
Or some sort of fraternity party or something.

No, it was a jam session. Because around in the 50s, in the 40s, 49 or 48 or something like that, every, uh, fraternity parties and all like that. Yeah. I had all that sold up up there. All on Jackson Avenue.
